headline: Dense fog gives way to a warm, dry start to the week; Central Kentucky rain chances return late Wednesday
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: An official Dense Fog Advisory remains in effect across Central Kentucky through 11 AM, with visibility near or below one-quarter mile in places. Fog and very low clouds should mix out from west to east this morning, followed by dry and much warmer weather today and Tuesday. Wednesday remains warm, but a few afternoon showers or thunderstorms may develop before rain chances increase Wednesday night.

currentConditions.wind: S 25 mph reported by the official feed

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: Official NWS Dense Fog Advisory through 11 AM; visibility may remain near or below one-quarter mile until fog lifts
days.forecast: Dense fog and very low ceilings continue through the morning commute. Fog should lift between midmorning and midday, revealing mostly sunny to partly cloudy skies. Southwest winds around 5–10 mph then support a quick warm-up into the lower 80s. Clear and mild conditions follow tonight.

days.label: Tuesday
days.forecast: Sunny, dry and unseasonably warm beneath strong upper-level ridging. Southwest winds around 5–10 mph accompany afternoon temperatures in the middle to upper 80s. Mostly clear and mild conditions continue Tuesday night.

days.label: Wednesday
days.precipitation: 10–20% during the afternoon; increasing to 40–55% Wednesday night
days.hazard: No official NWS alert at issuance; isolated thunderstorms and locally heavy downpours become possible Wednesday night
days.forecast: Mostly sunny, warm and humid through early afternoon. A weak disturbance may produce an isolated shower or thunderstorm after 2 PM, but most daytime hours remain dry. Shower and thunderstorm coverage increases Wednesday night as deeper moisture and additional disturbances approach from the west.

kentucky.bottomLine: Use extra caution in dense fog this morning. Once the fog lifts, today and Tuesday are dry and warm. Wednesday remains warm, with only a small daytime rain chance before showers and thunderstorms become more likely Wednesday night.
kentucky.confidence: High on fog lifting by midday and Tuesday's dry warmth; moderate-high on today's high temperature; moderate on Wednesday afternoon timing and nighttime rain coverage

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson / Central primary · Tempest excluded
upstate.summary: Clear and dry conditions have returned to Clemson and Central. Mostly sunny skies and light winds support afternoon temperatures in the lower to middle 80s today and Tuesday. Upper-level ridging strengthens Wednesday, producing another sunny and unseasonably warm day. No official NWS alerts were active for the Upstate at issuance.

currentConditions.condition: Network observations are WeatherFlow–Tempest-fed and excluded; official KCEU and KLQK observations used instead

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert; northwest gusts of 30–40 mph remain possible this morning along the higher Blue Ridge elevations, but advisory-level winds are not expected near Clemson and Central
days.forecast: Sunny, dry and warmer. Winds remain light near Clemson and Central, while higher ridges stay breezy through midday. Clear skies and light winds tonight support a wide local temperature spread between sheltered valleys and more exposed locations.

days.label: Tuesday
days.forecast: Sunny, dry and unseasonably warm. Light west winds accompany afternoon temperatures in the lower to middle 80s. Clear and mild conditions continue Tuesday night.

days.label: Wednesday
days.forecast: Sunny and very warm as upper-level ridging remains dominant across the Southeast. Winds stay light, with afternoon temperatures in the middle to upper 80s. Clear conditions continue Wednesday night.

upstate.bottomLine: The Upstate remains dry, sunny and unseasonably warm through Wednesday. Higher mountain ridges may be gusty this morning, but no significant weather hazards are expected near Clemson and Central.
upstate.confidence: High on the dry three-day forecast; high on Tuesday and Wednesday warmth; moderate-high on today's high because short-range guidance is slightly cooler than the official point forecast

sourceNotes: Official airport observations span 6:55–7:20 AM EDT. KDVK reported fog/mist with 0.75-mile visibility and a 100-foot ceiling, while KLEX reported fog with 0.25-mile visibility. KCEU and KLQK were clear with 10-mile visibility. No Tempest observations were used.

The NWS point forecasts were generated at 7:35 AM EDT. Danville has a high near 81°F today, 86°F Tuesday and 86°F Wednesday, with rain chances increasing from 20% Wednesday afternoon to 50% Wednesday night. Clemson has highs of 84°F today, 83°F Tuesday and 86°F Wednesday with essentially no rain.

Official hazards are distinct from the independent forecast: the Louisville Dense Fog Advisory remains in effect across Boyle, Fayette and surrounding counties through 11 AM. No official alert covered Clemson or Central at issuance.

The Louisville discussion expects widespread dense fog to lift from west to east this morning, followed by lower 80s in eastern Kentucky and warmer readings west. It highlights a very warm Tuesday and increasing but timing-dependent rain chances Wednesday into Thursday. The Greenville–Spartanburg discussion expects dry weather through the workweek, with 30–40 mph gusts confined mainly to higher elevations this morning.

Model inventories checked at 7:36 AM EDT showed complete 06Z HRRR through hour 48, 09Z RAP through hour 51, 06Z NAM through hour 84, 06Z NAM 3-km Nest through hour 60, 06Z GFS through hour 384, 06Z GEFS through hour 258 and complete 00Z ECMWF through hour 360. The 06Z ECMWF was not yet available.

College of DuPage radar at 7:30 AM EDT showed no precipitation across either forecast region. Clean-infrared imagery at 7:31 AM showed the former tropical cloud shield displaced well offshore, mostly clear inland conditions and only limited high cloud approaching from the west.

Short-range guidance supports rapid warming after fog erosion but is several degrees cooler near Clemson than the official point forecast. The Upstate range spans both clusters. GFS and ECMWF agree on widespread middle-80s Tuesday, while the Louisville discussion supports maintaining a warm Wednesday despite increasing moisture.

Clemson Weather Network identifies its observations as WeatherFlow–Tempest data. Those observations were excluded, and official KCEU and KLQK observations were used for Upstate analysis and verification.

The forecast-accuracy summary generated at 2:53 PM EDT October 11 was consulted. Central Kentucky daytime ranges were shifted modestly downward using KDVK's new recommended -1.5°F high correction, and overnight ranges used the recommended -2°F low correction. Upstate lows were widened because KCEU retains a recommended +1.5°F correction while KLQK retains a recommended -2.5°F correction.

HRRR remains the best overall high-temperature model with a 1.6°F mean absolute error, followed by RAP at 2.4°F. NAM has the best limited post-frontal-high-pressure score, so it received added weight today. Ranges remain broad because overall coverage is 58.3% and 72-hour coverage is 53.8%. Very low precipitation probabilities are consistent with the 12.3% observed frequency in the 0–20% reliability bin. This candidate does not modify the repository, forecast archive, website or widget.

appliedAdjustments.details: Shifted daytime ranges modestly downward using KDVK's new recommended -1.5°F high correction and shifted the lower portion of overnight ranges downward using its recommended -2°F low correction. KLEX remains below both correction thresholds. Wednesday's range remains wider because 72-hour coverage is only 53.8% and disturbance timing is uncertain.

Widened overnight ranges in both directions because KCEU has a recommended +1.5°F low correction while KLQK has a recommended -2.5°F correction. No daytime station correction qualified. HRRR received the greatest overall model weight, while NAM received added weight for today's post-frontal-high-pressure regime.
